transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Nguyen (Redwood SE), Elena Park (Redwood Solutions), Maya Singh (NovaBank ML), Carlos Ruiz (NovaBank Infra), Priya Menon (NovaBank Security), Aaron Lee (NovaBank Product)

Summary (auto-generated): Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize quantization profiles, demo of benchmark comparisons INT8 vs FP8, discussion of latency vs quality tradeoffs and pilot next steps.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'm Samir from Redwood, i'll hand over to jules for the deep dive on quantization but quickly - main goal today is to show tradeoffs between int8 and fp8 profiles and what you might expect for latency and quality tradeoffs with your workloads.
[00:18] Maya: thanks, yeah we are particularly concerned about any hallucination or instruction-following regressions when moving to int8.
[00:24] Jules: totally makes sense, we'll show both perf numbers and the quality evals we ran on a couple of instruction-following test sets. note, these are representative; we definitely want to run them on your prompts.
[00:35] Carlos: also we need to understand infra constraints — do we need special kernels or drivers for fp8? our infra team is fairly conservative.
[00:42] Jules: short answer — fp8 does require newer backend support; depending on GPU you may need newer CUDA/rocm builds and our runtime picks kernels at compile time. int8 tends to be more portable across fleet, but fp8 gives better quality/latency sweet spot in some models.
[00:56] Priya: quick sec — from security perspective, what telemetry and logs are collected during a pilot? we need to ensure no sensitive PII leaves scope.
[01:05] Samir: yeah we'll share the telemetry matrix and options — we can mask or drop inputs, and you can run pilot in Private mode or Dedicated to keep data inside your VPC. we'll share SOC2 and kms integration docs after the call.
[01:20] Aaron: can you show the actual benchmark charts?
[01:23] Jules: sure, pulling up the Optimize deck (link: https://redwood.example.com/deck/optimize-quant-profiles) — ok slide 3 shows quality vs latency curves for a 13B instruction-tuned model. you'll see fp8 points cluster close to fp16 quality but with lower latency; int8 points are faster but sometimes show a mild drop in Rouge/EM for certain instructions.
[01:45] Maya: is the quality metric automated or human-eval?
[01:49] Jules: mix — we run a token-level perplexity and an instruction-following automated metric, then a small human eval sample for edge cases. important caveat: automated metrics don't always capture user-critical failures.
[02:05] Carlos: the p95 latency numbers look pretty different when you enable batching. are those interactive numbers?
[02:10] Jules: good catch — the chart compares single-request latency (no batching) and a separate chart for throughput with typical batching (batch sizes 2-8). batching reduces per-token cost and increases throughput, but if you need strict p95 low-latency for UI, you tilt config to smaller batches and warm KV caches.
[02:27] Unknown Speaker 1: (murmur) yep
[02:30] Jules: also worth noting, KV cache warmup matters a lot — for chat-like workloads where prefixes repeat, caching can shave 20-40% off token generation time for subsequent requests. that's independent of quantization but interacts with it.
[02:45] Maya: do you have an example where int8 fails often? any concrete failure modes?
[02:50] Jules: yeah, int8 sometimes struggles on very narrow instruction-following where the model must be precise (e.g., exact table generation, strict code outputs). you'll see more token-level noise — which can be mitigated by selective-use: e.g., run the cheaper int8 profile for most calls and fallback to fp8/fp16 for critical endpoints or high-importance prompts.
[03:10] Samir: that's also why Optimize provides routing policies and automatic fallback — you can set cost thresholds or quality checks that route to fallback model variants.
[03:18] Carlos: regarding deployment, if we run Dedicated does that avoid the need to share telemetry with Redwood?
[03:23] Samir: Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and data plane that stays in your VPC; the control plane still interacts with Redwood for management unless you choose Private on-prem. we can present the exact network diagram in the security pack.
[03:37] Priya: KMS integration — does Redwood support BYOK with HSM-backed keys?
[03:42] Jules: yes we support KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys for private deployments; we'll send the spec.
[03:46] Maya: what about model rollbacks? if we see a regression in quality after quantization update, how fast can we rollback?
[03:52] Jules: rollbacks are immediate at the config layer — you pin the model version and quantization profile; fallback policy can be automatic if quality metrics drop below threshold, and we can orchestrate an immediate rollback. the main delay might be in cache warmup as the model variant changes.
[04:07] Aaron: can we get an estimate of cost delta — like int8 vs fp8 per 1M tokens?
[04:11] Samir: rough numbers in the deck, but general guidance: int8 often reduces per-token cost by 25-45% vs fp16; fp8 lands between int8 and fp16 depending on throughput. exact numbers depend on batching and model. we'll send a cost worksheet with your estimated QPS.
[04:25] Maya: i'd like to see results on our prompts — that's the only way to know if instruction-following drops matter.
[04:30] Samir: agreed — next step is we run a pilot using a NovaBank prompt set. jules will run perf+quality runs and share raw logs and a summary.
[04:38] Jules: quick note: for the pilot we recommend three buckets — cold start interactive flows, chat with repeated prefixes (to test KV cache), and high-throughput batch inference.
[04:46] Carlos: are there any special tuning knobs we should be aware of? quantization-aware layer selection?
[04:50] Jules: yes, Optimize supports selective layer quantization, per-layer scale tuning, and dynamic padding strategies. those are advanced knobs we can try if baseline int8 is borderline.
[04:59] Priya: regarding compliance, can logs be redacted on ingestion?
[05:02] Samir: yes, redaction hooks are available and we can run the pilot with redaction turned on; we just need your rules.
[05:09] Aaron: timeline-wise, we want a pilot in the next 2-3 weeks if possible.
[05:13] Samir: that's reasonable. jules, can you own the runbook?
[05:16] Jules: yes i will own it and share steps + infra checklist.
[05:20] Maya: great — please include eval scripts so we can reproduce metrics internally.
[05:24] Samir: will do. last thing, pricing for Dedicated — we'll include pilot pricing and committed terms in the follow-up.
[05:31] Maya: ok thanks all.
